claims.text: The House adopted the Burlison amendment on 22 July 2026 as an amendment to the FY2027 NDAA, establishing a permanent UAP Records Collection at the National Archives, an independent Senate-confirmed UAP Records Review Board with subpoena authority, statutory agency transfer timelines, and disclosure requirements extending to covered government contractors.

b.label: FY2027 NDAA as reported (S. 4784, S. Rept. 119-127)

edges.label: House-adopted amendment against a Senate base text with no UAP provisions
edges.note: The House framework must survive conference against a Senate reported bill (S. 4784, S. Rept. 119-127) containing zero UAP provisions - the second consecutive cycle in which the subject is absent from the Senate base text. The 2023 precedent is that the eminent-domain and review-board provisions were stripped in conference.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

edges.label: the successor framework, and the first time such a text has cleared the House floor
edges.note: Adopted by the House on 22 July 2026 as an amendment to the FY2027 NDAA, after a similar proposal failed to advance in the previous defence-bill cycle. As of this pass it is an adopted House amendment, not law, which is precisely the status distinction this domain is for.

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: Would impose statutory transfer timelines on the NARA collection
edges.note: The amendment requires agencies to identify, organise, preserve and transmit UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline and creates a Senate-confirmed Records Review Board with subpoena authority.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

edges.label: Statutory backstop for an executive release programme
edges.note: Burlison's own release frames the amendment as supporting PURSUE; structurally it cures each of PURSUE's defects - no timeline, no subpoena power, no reach to contractors, no Senate-confirmed decision-maker.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

edges.label: would reach contractor holdings
edges.note: The amendment extends disclosure requirements to covered government contractors - the only instrument that would reach the holdings Burlison sought from MITRE by letter in May 2026.

edges.label: the chamber where the text was stripped in 2023 and where a successor passed in 2026
edges.note: The House is where UAP oversight became public through the July 2023 Oversight hearing, where House leadership's role in the conference removal of the disclosure title became a contested question, and where the Burlison amendment was adopted on 22 July 2026. Both the defeat and the advance ran through the same chamber.
